CollaborationsCHEMISTRY OF
Chemistry is never the work of one element alone. It is the outcome of 
many strengths coming together with precision, purpose and possibility.
Our long-term contracts tell the same story
A 15-year backward integration arrangement with a leading global 
chemical major.  A multi-year agrochemical intermediates supply agreement.At Aarti Industries Limited (AIL), this idea goes beyond science. It shapes the way we think, partner and create value. Chemistry of Collaboration reflects our belief that meaningful progress is built when expertise meets trust, innovation meets execution, and shared ambition is sustained through long-term commitment.
This philosophy is reflected in 
our strategic collaborations.
Strategic collaborations are strengthening 
AIL’s supply chain resilience and partnership-led growth of key specialty chemical. With Superform Chemistries Limited, through Augene Chemical Pvt. Ltd., we are advancing joint development and manufacturing. With Re Sustainability and Recycling Pvt. Ltd. (RESL), and Aarti Circularity Limited, Wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, we are connecting chemistry with circularity through plastic materials recycling facilities and advanced circular materials. These initiatives are supported by long-term sourcing contracts, backward integration, diversified procurement & strategic inventory planning and cost effective operations. Each shared goal brings us 
closer to the future we are building.
At AIL, collaboration is more than a way of working. It is the chemistry 
through which science finds direction, partnerships find purpose and possibilities become lasting value.
Each collaboration adds a new dimension.
Each partnership deepens our relevance.

stakeholders as key partners in creating long-term, sustainable value. Our approach to engagement emphasises meaningful and transparent relationships, which are essential for building business resilience and trust. By using structured channels and feedback mechanisms, we keep stakeholders informed and engaged, incorporating their input into our sustainability agenda and adaptability.

The architecture of global 
manufacturing is being fundamentally redrawn. As global supply chains undergo their most dramatic and permanent realignment in decades, the world is actively seeking manufacturing partners defined by scale, scientific capability, and, most importantly, institutional reliability. In this historic transition, India has emerged not just as an alternative but as the strategic epicentre of the future of global speciality chemicals.
As we look ahead to the next phase 
of growth at Aarti Industries Limited (AIL), I am filled with profound pride, immense gratitude, and boundless optimism. From our origins as a modest manufacturing unit navigating a complex domestic economy four decades ago, we have methodically evolved into a forward-ready, globally respected enterprise. This remarkable transformation has been shaped by the enduring resilience of our teams, a shared vision of scientific excellence, and an unwavering belief in the vast potential of the Indian chemical sector.
Today, as India assumes an 
increasingly central role in global manufacturing and supply chains, we see a defining opportunity not just to participate in this shift but to help shape it in a meaningful and responsible manner. The next phase of industrial growth will be defined not only by scale and capability, but by trust, reliability, and the ability to build 
resilient global partnerships. 
We are no longer merely participating 
in India’s growth story; we are helping shape its foundation by bringing global collaboration to India and taking Indian capabilities to the world.
At AIL, we view this responsibility 
through a long-term lens in which growth is anchored in discipline, partnerships are built on trust, and progress is guided by a deep sense of accountability to all stakeholders. Our role extends beyond manufacturing; it is about contributing to global value chains in a manner that is dependable, responsible, and future-ready. 
Anchoring Our Future in 
Resilience and Core Values
Our decades-long journey has been 
guided by our commitment to our core values of Care, Integrity, and Excellence. These values are not mere corporate slogans; they have been our operational compass, steering us safely through the complexities of global supply disruptions, heightened geopolitical tensions, and highly volatile commodity cycles over the past few years. When external pressure mounts, our foundational value system ensures we honour our commitments, thereby cementing the deep, generational trust our 
customers place in us.
At AIL, we firmly believe that culture 
is our most enduring competitive advantage. This belief has guided our sustained focus on building an engaged, empowered, and aligned organisation. I am particularly proud that this commitment was recognised globally this year, as Aarti Industries was honoured with the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award. This recognition reflects the strong cultural foundation we have consciously built over time.
At the heart of this journey is our 
Aarti Engaging Leader model, which places people at the centre of our growth philosophy. Our leaders are encouraged to remain closely connected to their teams, foster open dialogue, value diverse perspectives, and create an environment where individuals feel confident to question the status quo. This has enabled us to strengthen engagement year after year, while building a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
What stands out most is the 
alignment across our organisation, across functions, levels, and geographies, where teams are united by a shared purpose and a collective commitment to excellence. This cultural cohesion has translated into Dear Stakeholders,We are entering a defining era for the Indian 
manufacturing where trust, innovation, and scientific excellence will define global leadership, and Aarti Industries is proud to help shape that future.
Rajendra Gogri

continuous improvement, while reinforcing the trust placed in us by our stakeholders.

FY26 was a year of resilience and 
calibrated recovery for Aarti Industries Limited (AIL), as we navigated a highly volatile global environment and delivered improved sequential performance throughout the year. Our revenues stood at ` 9,018 Crs, with EBITDA of ` 1,172 Crs, and margins stabilising in the latter half, supported by disciplined execution and agile commercial strategies. Reflecting on FY26, our performance profoundly underscores the structural resilience and operational agility we have meticulously embedded across every level of AIL. I am particularly proud of how our teams responded to an exceptionally challenging environment with agility, ownership, and a strong commitment to execution. 
In a year characterised by a highly 
complex, fragmented global environment, persistent geopolitical friction, and rapidly shifting supply-demand equations, we recognised early on that traditional operating models would no longer suffice. We adopted a deliberate, execution-focused paradigm to navigate this volatility: Chemistries of Collaboration.
At AIL, we believe that collaboration 
is not just an internal theme or a catchphrase; it is a core strategic and financial enabler. It represents the deliberate synergy among our highly flexible manufacturing assets, disciplined capital allocation frameworks, and deep, long-term 
alignments with global customers. This integrated approach has enabled us to improve capacity utilisation to about 80% across all key products, enhance customer stickiness, and strengthen margin resilience across key business segments. 
Driven by our core cultural bedrock 
of Care, Integrity, and Excellence, our exceptional team of over 5,800+ professionals demonstrated that true commitment to operational rigour extends beyond our gates. Their resilience and commitment ensured business continuity, customer reliability, and operational excellence even during periods of heightened uncertainty. It enables us to forge strategic alliances, co-create complex chemical solutions, and definitively position AIL as the Global Partner of Choice in the speciality chemicals sector.
Safety remains our highest priority. 
During the year, we continued to strengthen our safety systems, processes, and on-ground practices, with a sharp focus on behavioural safety and operational discipline.  Our Total Recordable Incident Frequency Rate (TRIFR) of 1.15 stands significantly below the industry benchmark (~2.0), reinforcing our dedication to maintaining a zero-harm workplace across every manufacturing facility. Environmental stewardship remains 
central to our growth strategy and long-term value creation. Our progress is reflected in the recognition we continue to receive from global ESG assessment platforms. During the year, Aarti Industries achieved the prestigious EcoVadis Platinum rating , placing us in the top 1% of companies globally. We were also included in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026 for the second consecutive year, achieving the highest score among Indian chemical companies. In addition, we retained Leadership ratings in CDP Climate Change and CDP Water Security, CDP supply chain, reaffirming our commitment to environmental excellence, sustainable growth , transparency, and responsible business practices
I am exceptionally proud that this 
high-performance, people-centric operational culture has gained global recognition, with AIL being named a 2026 Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award winner. This accolade confirms that our investments in capability building, safety, and employee empowerment are yielding a highly engaged workforce capable of navigating unprecedented industry complexities and exceptional performance.

Looking Ahead: Capital 
Allocation and Our Strategy for FY27
As our multi-year Capex cycle 
concludes, we are shifting focus towards maximising asset utilisation and improving capital efficiency. Our strategic priority is to drive a higher contribution from advanced materials and specialty products.
We will maintain a disciplined capital 
allocation approach, with a minimum pre-tax ROCE threshold of 20% for new investments. Our current ROCE stands at approximately 8%, and we are committed to improving it through higher utilisation, a better product mix, and operational efficiencies.
We are also focused on strengthening 
the balance sheet. Our net debt-to-EBITDA stands at 3.7x, and we are targeting a reduction to <2.5x over the next 12-24 months through strong free cash flow generation. We expect FY27 to deliver improved utilisation, margin expansion, and a meaningful inflexion in free cash flows.
We step into the next phase with 
strong conviction in our strategy and execution capabilities. Our focus remains on delivering consistent, profitable growth, robust cash flows and superior shareholder returns. We remain committed to building Aarti Industries into a globally trusted partner that creates long-term, compounding value for all stakeholders.
I sincerely thank our employees, 
customers, partners, investors and the Board for their continued trust, commitment and support as we shape AIL’s next phase of growth together.
Sincerely,
Suyog Kotecha

Strategic Execution: The 
Unmatched Power of Partnerships
FY26 was a pivotal year for 
executing forward integration and commercialising the significant capital investments we have made over the past strategic cycle. The year also unfolded against a backdrop of global volatility, marked by shifting trade dynamics, tariff uncertainty, raw material fluctuations and increasing customer expectations around supply security. This environment reinforced the importance of partnerships that go beyond transactional supply and create greater certainty across sourcing, manufacturing, commercialisation and long-term demand visibility.
Our state-of-the-art Zone IV 
facility at Jhagadia is successfully transitioning from a construction site to a commercial powerhouse. Highlighted by the commissioning Navigating Headwinds 
with Agility and Unyielding Discipline
FY26 rigorously tested our 
organisational flexibility and our stress threshold. We began the year facing a confluence of severe external disruptions. These included profound geopolitical shifts that disrupted global logistics networks, extreme volatility in raw material prices, particularly sharp, unpredictable corrections in upstream derivatives such as benzene and aniline, and the sudden imposition of new U.S. tariffs that threatened our established export corridors.
Rather than adopting a defensive 
posture or waiting for the macro-environment to naturally correct itself, we relied heavily on our execution discipline. We initiated comprehensive, structural cost-optimisation programmes across our entire value chain. By establishing a lean, highly efficient operational baseline, optimising our procurement strategies, and implementing dynamic pricing models, we successfully limited the deterioration in profitability during the most volatile quarters. This is reflected in EBITDA margins stabilising at ~13% to 14% and improving sequentially in the second half of the year. 
When faced with localised 
disruptions, our commercial teams demonstrated remarkable agility. They swiftly recalibrated global trade flows, actively scaling our presence and market share in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa to offset localised softness elsewhere. We did not abandon our key markets; instead, we worked collaboratively with our North American partners to actively absorb parts of the new U.S. tariffs. Exports accounted for approximately 57% of total revenues, with the U.S. market experiencing a gradual recovery in volumes during the year. Internally, we focused relentlessly on 
future-proofing our enterprise against inevitable future shocks. By deploying advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital twins, and predictive maintenance tools across our critical process blocks, we have transitioned from reactive to proactive plant management. 
We are now driving measurable  
gains, including:
100+ Cr (Variable and Fixed) cost 
improvement 
30%+ Y-o-Y Volume growth Coupled with our accelerating 
transition to hybrid renewable energy, we are structurally reducing our baseline operating costs while simultaneously achieving our carbon footprint reduction targets.  
Accelerating Our 
Green Transition:  
We are on track to have our hybrid 
renewable energy portfolio exceed 75% of our total power purchases across key facilities by Q1 FY27, while significantly reducing our carbon footprint and operating costs.
Evolving in a Dynamic Global 
Landscape
As the year progressed, we witnessed 
profound structural shifts in global trade that strategically favour India as a manufacturing hub and AIL, specifically, as a preferred partner. The successful conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and positive, ongoing developments in U.S.-India trade dynamics are structurally lowering tariff barriers for high-end specialty chemicals, opening up entirely new, highly lucrative corridors for our Advanced Materials portfolio. We are actively engaging with customers across these regions, with a strong pipeline of product qualifications and commercial discussions underway. We are also closely monitoring 
China’s evolving industrial policy. Historically, excess capacity and aggressive export pricing impacted global margins. Recent policy shifts aimed at rationalising domestic competition are expected to restore pricing discipline. We expect gradual normalisation in pricing over the next 12-24 months, supporting margin recovery for global specialty chemical players. 
In this environment, customer 
expectations are evolving from transactional sourcing to strategic partnerships. Our integrated value chain model positions us strongly to deliver reliability, compliance, and supply chain resilience.
Delivering Value: Sweating 
Assets and Monumental Strategic Wins
Our financial and operational 
momentum recovered strongly as we progressed through FY26, a direct result of our conscious strategy to maximise throughput from our existing assets. We improved asset turns and increased utilisation across key product chains. 
Our energy-linked portfolio, 
particularly MMA, achieved its highest-ever volumes. We are scaling fuel additives capacities from 290 KTPA to 360 KTPA by year-end. “In a world of shifting trade 
dynamics, our ability to seamlessly partner with global innovators, local suppliers, and international customers has proven to be our strongest strategic moat. We are not just supplying chemicals; we are co-creating absolute supply chain resilience.”

Shri Chandrakant V. Gogri
Chairman Emeritus
Shri Chandrakant V. Gogri is the architect of Aarti Industries 
Limited’s growth journey, bringing deep expertise across chemical manufacturing, operations and marketing. An alumnus of ICT, formerly UDCT, with a degree in Chemical Engineering, he founded Aarti Industries Limited and played a defining role in shaping it from a single manufacturing unit into a globally recognised enterprise.
After serving as the Founding Chairman, he stepped down 
from the role in 2012 and continues to guide the Company as Chairman Emeritus, offering strategic direction, institutional wisdom and long-term perspective.
His contribution to the chemical industry has been widely 
recognised through several distinguished honours. These include the Chemexcil Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025, the Lifetime Contribution Award at the Chemical and Petrochemical Awards by FICCI, the D. M. Trivedi Lifetime Achievement Award from ICC, the Lala Shriram National Award for Leadership in the Chemical Industry, and the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Gujarat Dyestuff Manufacturers Association.

Built on Integration, 
Expanded by Innovation
With 16 manufacturing plants, 100+ 
products, 4 R&D centres (including 2 pilot plants) and over 250 scientists, AIL combines scale with scientific depth. Its Zone IV platform at Jhagadia further enhances flexibility, supporting advanced materials, specialised downstream products and faster commercialisation of molecules.
Trusted across  
Markets
AIL serves 1,100+ domestic and global 
customers across 60+ countries. Its strategically located manufacturing footprint in Western India, close to key ports, enables efficient servicing of both domestic and export markets.Future-ready  
by Design
As it prepares for the future, AIL 
is advancing multiple priorities. Strengthening circularity, while digital transformation and AI-enabled initiatives improve operational intelligence and efficiency. Sustainability programmes continue to advance responsible manufacturing. Guided by Care, Integrity and Excellence, AIL is building an agile, higher-value platform for sustainable growth.Positioned 
as a Global 
AIL is more than a speciality chemicals manufacturer. It is an 
integrated chemistry partner, supporting global customers across complex, high-value and reliability-critical applications.
From Supply to 
Strategic Collaboration
Beyond manufacturing, AIL’s 
relationships increasingly extend across feedstock security, technology sharing, joint development, manufacturing outsourcing and market access. This integrated approach continues to strengthen customer and partner relationships while creating mutual value across the value chain.
Recent milestones include a USD 150 
million multi-year supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator, a 15-year backward integration arrangement with a global chemical major, and an exclusive Actylis distribution agreement for PCBTF in the US coatings market.
Alongside these strategic partnerships, 
Aarti Industries is strengthening supply security by developing alternate sourcing avenues for critical feedstocks such as benzene, sulfur and methanol, while maintaining planned inventory buffers for key imported materials, including one-and-a-half to two months of aniline stock.Established in 1984 by first-generation 
technocrats, AIL has evolved into a diversified speciality chemicals platform with deep expertise across Benzene and Toluene value chains. Its capabilities span nitration, chlorination, hydrogenation, ethylation and downstream chemistries, enabling the Company to serve diverse end-use industries, including agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, polymers, energy applications, dyes and pigments, paints, coatings and advanced materials.The Partner behind 
Critical ChemistriesPartner of Choice
Sustainability by Design
Sustainability is embedded in the 
Company’s operating philosophy. It is advancing waste-to-value programmes, exploring bio-based feedstocks and adopting circular chemistry processes to reduce environmental impact while unlocking new opportunities for responsible growth.
Digitally 
Enabled Innovation
At its digitised R&D centre in Navi 
Mumbai, the Company is leveraging advanced analytics and digital tools to improve process efficiency, strengthen decision-making and mitigate supply chain risks. This digital foundation is helping create a faster, smarter and more resilient innovation ecosystem.Built to Scale 
New Chemistries
The Company’s ambition to become 
a global partner of choice is anchored in next-generation manufacturing capabilities that enable entry into new markets with speed and confidence. At the heart of this journey is its multi-purpose and new process blocks at Zone IV facility, expected to commercialise in FY27. Equipped with a pilot plant, continuous processing units and automated distillation technologies, the unit is designed to accelerate the scale-up of new chemistries and enable faster ramp-up.Collaboration as a 
Growth Engine

Company’s value creation approach. It is working towards long-term agreements with CDMOs and contract manufacturing partners to drive co-innovation and accelerate the development of high-value chemicals. The Aarti Industries:
ChemistryBuilt on
CollaborationStrengthened byBusiness Overview
 AIL is a global 
leader in speciality chemicals, where the Chemistry of Collaboration powers world-class process innovation, scalable engineering, and sustainable value creation.
Over four decades, AIL has evolved 
through enduring partnerships, building a diversified portfolio spanning basic and speciality chemicals and advanced intermediates. The Company specialises in complex, multi-step chemistries, including chlorination, nitration, hydrogenation, diazotisation, fluorination, ammonolysis, and photochemistry amongst many others. These capabilities enable the development of value-added intermediates across applications.
AIL operates as a long-term strategic 
partner, defined by scientific rigour, operational reliability, and solution-led innovation. Its facilities, processes, and people are aligned to deliver consistent performance.

Engineering Sustainable Growth
AIL is moving from capacity-led expansion towards selective, higher-value and innovation-led growth. Its strategy 
combines advanced chemistries, flexible manufacturing, strategic partnerships and disciplined execution.Strategic Direction
AIL’s strategy connects advanced chemistries, flexible manufacturing, long-term partnerships, digitalisation and disciplined capital allocation to drive higher-value growth and improved returns.
Move towards 
Advanced Chemistries
AIL is expanding into application-led 
chemistries with stronger entry barriers. FY27 commissioning includes the

Existing Assets
AIL is improving asset productivity 
through better yields, energy and steam optimisation, procurement efficiencies, renewable power and product-market optimisation.

What Drives 
At Aarti Industries, 
the ESG strategy is guided by a materiality assessment that identifies the environmental, social, and governance issues most relevant to long-term value creation. The process is built on stakeholder inputs, bringing together diverse perspectives to define priorities and focus action on areas of highest impact, supporting responsible growth. 
The assessment is reviewed 
annually to remain aligned with strategic priorities, emerging risks, and regulatory developments. In addition, a comprehensive evaluation is undertaken every three years, incorporating inputs from internal and external stakeholders.Since fiscal year 2019, we have conducted these assessments annually. In FY24, we conducted a double materiality assessment based on the GRI 2021 framework, collaborating with a third-party consultant to gather insights from our stakeholders. 
In FY26, the identified material topics were reassessed for both impact and 
financial relevance, with no changes identified. Accordingly, the materiality matrix remained unchanged. 
The Company engaged extensively with stakeholders to gather their insights 
on the material issues for its ESG strategy. The materiality assessment is subsequently reviewed and approved by the Finance and Investment Committee prior to the sign off by the Board of Directors. 
Understanding Double Materiality
Financial Materiality:
Assesses how external factors influence the Company’s financial performance, including related risks and opportunities (outside-in), across the short, medium, and long term.Impact Materiality:
Assesses how the Company’s operations affect people, society, and the environment (inside-out), across the short, medium, and long term.
Approach to Double Materiality
AIL’s double materiality framework enables the Company to identify and prioritise ESG issues and opportunities that are relevant to both business performance and stakeholder impact.
The assessment is aligned with the GRI Standards 2021 and the Corporate 
Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). Since FY24, it reflects a dual perspective, covering both impact and financial materiality, and linking ESG priorities to long-term value creation.C11

Risk Management Framework and Risk Management Process
Risk management is a continuous process embedded across our organisation. Our framework focuses on identifying, 
prioritising, managing and reviewing risks to enable timely mitigation and reporting. We align our approach with the COSO framework, integrating risk management with business strategy and compliance, which enhances our ability to spot emerging risks and opportunities. The framework outlines governance structures and stakeholder roles and implements policies to minimise financial and operational risks. Our Board-approved Risk Management Policy assesses key material risks and emphasises prudent practices for managing our risk profile, combining both quantitative and qualitative data for a comprehensive approach.
Risk Management Process
In FY26, the Risk Management Committee held two meetings to review the policy and systems. ERM training covered functional and cross-functional risks.

Foresight for a 
At Aarti Industries Limited, risk management (RM) is integrated into 
decision-making to support strategic goals. It is an integral part of how we evaluate and respond to evolving business conditions. The Risk Management Policy supports sustainable growth, operational efficiency and stakeholder value creation through a structured approach to risk identification, assessment and mitigation. Aligned with the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI LODR, ISO 31000:2018 and COSO principles, it includes regular maintenance of risk registers and databases to enable informed decision-making. The policy is reviewed by the Board once every two years or earlier, in response to specific events or developments.  
Risk Governance
We follow a three-tier governance structure for effective risk oversight and management:
Board 
Oversight
The Board, led by the Chairman, 
oversees enterprise risk through 
a Board-level Risk Management 
Committee (RMC) comprising 
Independent, Non-Executive, and 
Executive Directors, ensuring balanced 
oversight. The RMC aligns risk strategy 
with business objectives, identifies 
emerging risks, and reviews the risk 
profile and mitigation plans half-yearly, 
reporting to the Board. The RMC is 
supported by the Audit Committee 
at the Board level which oversees 
financial risks and internal controls, 
ensuring comprehensive coverage.Management-Level 
Governance
The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) 
implements risk policies and serves 
as the link between the RMC and 
plant-level risk owners. Working 
with functional leaders, the CRO 
ensures consistent risk identification, 
mitigation and compliance across 
the organisation, reports to the CEO, 
and is accountable to the RMC on risk 
matters.Working 
Group
Function Heads, as Risk Owners, 
manage operational risks within 
their areas, supported by teams that 
identify, assess and mitigate emerging 
risks in line with AIL’s objectives. 
Internal audit reviews compliance 
and risk management against Board 
policies, while external audits provide 
an independent evaluation. The 
framework reinforces accountability 
and ownership through ongoing audit 
oversight.

Risk Culture
AIL institutionalises a risk-aware 
culture that transforms risk management from a compliance process into an organisation-wide mindset. Continuous risk and sustainability briefings are delivered to the Board of Directors and Independent Directors through interactive leadership sessions, expert forums, and operational plant tours. Using the specialised Aarti Online Training Modules (ATOMs) platform, compliance modules covering the Code of Conduct, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC), and Whistleblower protocols are mandatory for 100% of the workforce. 100% of eligible employees undergo mandatory information security modules and annual training refreshers to protect data privacy and secure corporate intellectual property.For our shop-floor employees field-level risk awareness is actively reinforced for frontline chemical associates through simulation-driven Safety Action Meetings (SAM), Continuous Learning from Incidents (LFI), and strict field competency assessments.
Driven by our value of Integrity,  
accountability is hardwired into AIL’s human resource infrastructure by seamlessly linking risk metrics, compliance protocols and safety targets directly to corporate remuneration structures. Senior management performance goals are directly bound to Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), risk mitigation tracking, and the fulfillment of safety and environmental parameters. Achieving or missing critical safety and environmental objectives directly influences executive variable pay and performance appraisals, building a culture of continuous containment.
Risk Audits
AIL continuously monitors the effectiveness of its control systems through an independent risk audit architecture. An in-house internal audit department systematically conducts continuous, risk-based operational reviews to monitor internal financial controls and trace policy deviations. Independent third-party audits of the overarching risk management processes and non-financial sustainability metrics are conducted once every two years. The Audit Committee and Risk Management Committee operate rigorous reporting channels to ensure the Board remains informed of material issues, committee performance, and the remediation track of responsible employees.Aarti Industries Limited operates a proactive Enterprise-wide Risk Management (ERM) framework to systematically identify, analyse, quantify, treat, and monitor strategic, operational, financial, compliance, and emerging sustainability risk exposures, ensuring long-term business continuity and operational stability.
AIL deploys an integrated hybrid risk identification structure:
Top-Down 
Strategic Assessment
The Board-level Risk Management 
Committee (RMC) and senior leadership 
analyse macroeconomic shifts, trade 
dynamics, geopolitical uncertainties, 
and long-term climate transition 
risks to align corporate strategy with 
global realities.Bottom-Up

capture process-level hazards,

dynamically escalating ground-level 
data into functional risk registers.
Risk Quantification and Appetite 
Identified risks are mathematically evaluated using a standardised 5 x 5 Risk Score Matrix, where the absolute score 
is a multiple of Likelihood (Rare 1 to Near Certain 5) and Impact (Insignificant 1 to Critical 5). This data-driven scoring framework factors in quantitative and qualitative implications, including impacts on EBITDA, market share volatility, human safety, environmental degradation, and brand reputation. AIL relies on continuous scenario modelling, stress testing, and industry benchmarking to validate mitigation barriers against volatility. Our Risk Appetite Framework sets clear tolerance boundaries mapped against specific matrix segments:
Risk Escalation and 
Governance 
Any material risk breaching the high-
exposure threshold (Score 15-25) is instantly flagged by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) and functional Risk Owners, and escalated to the RMC semi-annually to enforce corrective mitigation and stress-testing. Functional Heads and Risk Owners update department-specific risk registers and submit progress metrics to executive management. The Board-level RMC formally reviews corporate risk maps, prioritised exposures, and control barriers twice a year to provide strategic governance assurance. The Board of Directors independently re-evaluates the overarching Risk Management Policy at least once every two years, or dynamically in response to material regulatory or market trigger events.Low risk appetite for safety, regulatory and environmental compliance, ethics, and human rights
High risk appetite for innovation and 
digitalisationModerate risk appetite for financial stewardship and strategic growth

Description
Structural volatility and policy shifts in key downstream sectors 
can trigger unpredictable demand contractions across specialised chemical applications.Description
The evolution of external Generative and Agentic AI tools is rapidly transforming chemical synthesis, process modeling, and operational workflows, threatening to make traditional manufacturing technologies and legacy digital platforms obsolete across the industry.Description
Global trade policy shifts, tariffs, and sanctions can hinder Aarti Industries’ access to raw materials and export markets. Regulatory restrictions and non-tariff barriers can raise costs and limit market reach, thereby impacting competitiveness and profit margins, particularly in areas with high regulatory volatility or geopolitical uncertainty.Description
Persistent global macroeconomic headwinds, structural overcapacity in key regional chemical hubs, and escalating trade protectionism threaten long-term industrial demand growth across key international markets.
Impact
Over-reliance on the energy segment, exposes earnings to volatility, tariff barriers, and regional off-take shifts, resulting in margin erosion and lower capacity utilisation.Impact
Delayed integration of agentic workflows could compress competitor R&D cycles and erode Aarti’s market edge in specialty intermediates. Operationally, it risks sub-optimal process yield optimisation and slower customer responsiveness, while increasing reliance on autonomous AI systems introduces unprecedented algorithmic governance, IP exposure, and specialised data privacy vulnerabilities.Impact
Trade tensions and tariffs can affect our product’s competitiveness in export markets. The EU is expected to introduce a carbon tax on chemical products in 3 to 5 years, potentially impacting our margins in line with existing rates for other sectors.Impact
These external economic risks are impacting export market volumes, compressing operating margins across core value chains, and lowering asset utilisation of existing manufacturing assets.
Mitigation
AIL mitigates this exposure through geographic market expansion, portfolio pivot, flexible multi-purpose asset deployment, and long-term off-take contracts to  de-risk revenue.Mitigation
AIL is proactively advancing its UNNATI and Aarti 4.0 strategic transformation by integrating Generative and Agentic AI across business processes to enhance yield, operational agility, and decision-making. The Company is scaling digital capabilities via predictive analytics and Digital Twins, while driving enterprise-wide capability building through digital upskilling programmes and a network of 100+ GenAI Champions. These deployment efforts are safeguarded by a robust Responsible AI framework, enterprise data governance, and enhanced cybersecurity protocols.Mitigation
We will have our strategy department monitor foreign trade policy and utilise free trade agreements. Additionally, we are collaborating with our business partners to increase the visibility of our carbon footprint throughout the supply chain.Mitigation
AIL mitigates this through strategic pivot into high-value advanced materials, leveraging flexible Zone IV multi-purpose assets, entering long-term off-take contracts, and expanding footprint in high-growth geographies.

ESG Journey: Governance, Strategy and the Road Ahead
Evolution
Over the years, AIL has strengthened its ESG approach, evolving from compliance-led actions to an integrated business 
priority. Responsible manufacturing now extends across environmental, social, and governance practices, shaping operations and long-term value creation.
ESG Governance
Strategy
At Aarti Industries Limited, ESG 
strategy and roadmaps are embedded across operations through an integrated, forward-looking approach that brings together business priorities, stakeholder expectations and emerging sustainability imperatives. Focus areas include fragmented data, evolving carbon policies, Scope 3 emissions and alignment with frameworks such as GRI, NGRBC, UN SDGs, UNGC and SASB, alongside disclosures including CDP , DJSI, EcoVadis and Sustainalytics. The Company also continues to strengthen ESG awareness across its supplier ecosystem, extending responsible practices beyond its own operations.
Progress across renewable 
energy, energy efficiency and water conservation reflects this commitment, with sustainability considerations integrated into new 
plant design. A third-party ESG gap assessment further supported risk identification, stakeholder engagement and the development of S.M.A.R.T. ESG and climate goals linked to executive compensation.
Key initiatives, including carbon 
reduction, workplace safety and community engagement, are aligned to defined pillars, strengthening accountability, transparency and shared ownership across the organisation.
Climate-related performance 
is integrated into employee performance management systems at AIL. Monetary incentives linked to sustainability, environmental and operational targets are considered for senior leadership, including the CEO, COOs and Zonal Operations Heads.Climate-related KPIs incorporated within AIL’s incentive framework include 
progress towards greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets. In line with its Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi)-approved commitments, AIL aims to reduce absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions by 54.6% and Scope 3 GHG emissions by 32.5% by FY33, using FY23 as the base year. Performance against these climate targets is considered in employee performance evaluations and influences variable compensation and performance ratings. 
In addition, recognition-based and non-
monetary incentives encourage wider employee participation in environmental priorities, including energy efficiency, water stewardship, waste reduction and emissions management. These incentives are aligned with AIL’s published targets under the respective capitals in this report.

Climate Governance
Board Oversight
The Chairman is accountable for climate-related initiatives, while the Board-level Risk Management Committee provides oversight of climate-related risks, opportunities, strategy, targets and performance. The Committee reviews climate-related performance on a quarterly basis and provides strategic guidance on climate-related policies and initiatives. The Risk Management Committee is supported by other Board committees, including the Audit Committee and Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee, on matters relevant to climate governance. 
Management-level GovernanceThe Apex Sustainability Council, comprising Executive Directors, C-suite officers and functional leaders, including the Head of Environment and Sustainability is responsible for managing climate-related issues across the Company. The Council oversees climate strategy, decarbonisation initiatives, GHG emissions reduction targets, climate-related risks and opportunities, and monitors progress against the Company’s sustainability and climate commitments. 
Sustainability KPIs are integrated into performance management across all levels, embedding climate priorities 
into day-to-day operations and encouraging continuous improvement.
Working GroupCorporate and site-level environment and sustainability teams support the execution of climate-related programmes, monitor progress against climate targets, and drive coordinated action across operational locations.

Near-Term Targets
As per its SBTi-approved targets, AIL commits to reducing absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 54.6% by FY33 from the FY23 base year. It also commits to reducing absolute Scope 3 emissions by 32.5% during the same period.
Following SBTi validation of its science-based targets, 
the Company is pursuing absolute GHG emission reductions. With 74% of energy currently coal-based, AIL is transitioning towards renewable and circular energy sources. Its approach integrates responsible procurement, supplier risk assessment, and alignment with the Paris Agreement, SBTi, and UN SDGs. The transition is being advanced in collaboration with partners across the value chain to support decarbonisation efforts.

CASE STUDY
SUPPORTING NET ZERO AND RESOURCE 
CIRCULARITY THROUGH INDUSTRY ADVOCACY
Aarti Industries actively 
supports India’s Net Zero 2070 vision by advocating for energy-efficient, climate-aligned industrial policies and is committed to achieve Net Zero by 2050. For coastal manufacturing installations, we recommend evaluating scientifically validated deep-sea discharge as a highly pragmatic, low-carbon alternative to traditional Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) frameworks. While ZLD remains crucial for conserving freshwater in inland regions, its intensive energy requirements significantly elevate carbon emissions. The carbon footprint of a ZLD system can be 7 to 14 times higher than that of marine discharge via pipeline. Even when factoring in transportation for facilities without direct pipeline access (up to 200 km), 
marine discharge still offers a substantial carbon-saving advantage. To responsibly implement this low-carbon transition, we support regulatory alignments such as revising coastal effluent inlet norms and expanding dedicated pipeline networks in key chemical clusters.
We actively advocate for 
simplified regulatory and compliance pathways under Rule 9 of the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016 to facilitate the seamless reclassification of industrial by-products as commercial resources rather than waste. This streamlined administrative framework accelerates industrial circularity by allowing valuable materials, such as spent hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4), to be safely recirculated back into the value chain. Ultimately, this cooperative policy effort reduces our industry's dependence on hazardous virgin acids, directly supports the local fertiliser manufacturing ecosystem, and prevents substantial volumes of waste generation. Using leading industry platforms like the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI) and the Indian Chemical Council (ICC), Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI).

Tax Strategy
Tax Principles
Anchored in integrity, excellence, and care. We do not 
transfer value created to low-tax jurisdictions.
Transparency and Reporting 
AIL adheres to open and transparent tax practices, including providing relevant and accurate information to tax authorities upon request.
Tax Governance
Guided by experienced teams, qualified professionals, and senior management and board-level oversight.
Tax Risk Mitigation Strategy
Proactively identifies and manages tax risks to support business objectives.
Compliance
Committed to comply with the spirit as well as the letter of tax laws and regulations in the countries we operate in. Ensure transfer pricing of intercompany transactions is in accordance with the arm’s length principle, ensuring compliance with local and international regulations.
Advocacy
Engages on policy matters through structured collaboration between advocacy and tax teams.
Engagement and Tax Authorities
Maintains transparent, fair, and collaborative interactions with tax authorities.
Tax Planning
Focused on efficient and compliant operations, supported by external expertise. Avoiding aggressive tax practices. We do engage in artificial or contrived tax arrangements or the use of tax havens for tax avoidance.

Collaborating for Manufacturing Excellence
Project Aarohan: Turning 
Process Knowledge into PerformanceProject Aarohan is a collaborative transformation initiative focused on driving operational excellence across our 
manufacturing network. It brings together process experts, plant teams and data and analytics specialists to improve yield, throughput, resource efficiency and operating discipline. Through the Real-Time Manufacturing Insight (RTMI) platform, live plant data is converted into actionable insights, enabling teams to identify constraints, test solutions and sustain improvements.
The programme combines technology with structured problem-solving. More than 50 employees from manufacturing 
locations were trained as change agents, while a four-member Data Scientist Cohort was developed to independently build, deploy and scale analytics solutions. This strengthens in-house capability and embeds evidence-based decision-making closer to operations.

Cross-functional teams use a common 
data environment to identify performance gaps, analyse root causes and translate insights into plant-level action. Training in data interpretation, process analytics, digital twins and predictive methods enables employees to solve recurring problems and replicate successful interventions across locations.Advanced analytics, combined with process expertise and disciplined execution, delivered ` 7.4 Crs in annualised benefit during FY26. Interventions included yield improvement, steam-efficiency enhancement and other operational improvements that reduced variability and strengthened asset utilisation. 
Together, these initiatives demonstrate that digital tools create lasting

While Aarohan builds data-led problem-solving capability across manufacturing, the Man-Tech Interface applies this combined expertise to specific process, product and plant challenges.How Collaboration Creates Value The Man-Tech Interface: Solving Plant Challenges Together
The Manufacturing-Technology 
(Man-Tech) Interface connects R&D, technology specialists, process chemists and plant engineers to resolve operational constraints and improve product and process performance. Teams use live plant data, process simulation, root-cause analysis and trials to convert technical insight into practical plant interventions. Yield and throughput:  fine-tuning 
operating conditions and reaction parameters to improve conversion and productivity.
 Targeted debottlenecking: identifying constraints across equipment, utilities and process steps to release capacity from existing assets. Resource efficiency: reducing energy, water and material intensity while supporting ESG priorities.
 Product quality and customer assurance: responding to evolving specifications through tighter process control and repeatable quality.The Interface Focuses on Four Outcomes
CASE STUDY
SECURING COLOUR IMPROVEMENT 
THROUGH PROCESS OPTIMISATION
Customer specifications for the colour profile of a product became more stringent. AIL needed a sustainable 
solution that protected optical purity without interrupting production or requiring major capital expenditure.The Challenge
Process chemists and plant engineers jointly mapped the reaction and downstream stages, analysed process data and tested alternatives. The team identified specific operating conditions during the reaction phase that prevented colour formation without affecting yield or optical purity.The Collaborative Solution
This intervention demonstrates how manufacturing experience, scientific expertise and customer requirements can be 
combined to resolve a technically complex challenge and build lasting process capability.The intervention met the revised specification without major capital expenditure or production disruption, strengthening AIL’s position as a reliable global supplier.OUTCOME

Expanding with Discipline and Operating through AMS
By involving operating and specialist teams from the design stage, AIL seeks to ensure that new capacity is not only 
commissioned efficiently but is also safer, more reliable and better positioned to deliver sustained value.
Delivering projects with discipline is only the first step. Projects integrate engineering, procurement, technology, 
manufacturing and SHE inputs from design through commissioning. HAZOP , QRA and LOPA studies, advanced process controls, lifecycle assessments and value engineering strengthen execution quality, risk control and future readiness. Sustaining their value requires a common operating system across sites, functions and teams.Execution ExcellenceThe Aarti Management System (AMS) creates a common operating rhythm across sites (Zones) through Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Morale and Environment (SQDCME). Daily visual management, tiered accountability meetings, root-cause analysis and real-time KPI reviews help teams identify deviations early, assign ownership and sustain improvement.
AMS connects site leadership, functional teams and frontline employees around four enterprise outcomes: prosperity, 
people well-being, partner delight and sustainability. By linking shop-floor action with strategic performance, it strengthens accountability, enables faster escalation and helps successful practices move across plants and functions. 
With this common operating rhythm in place, multidisciplinary teams can identify recurring constraints and redesign 
processes for safer, more efficient and more sustainable performance.Aarti Management System: One Operating Rhythm
AIL’s expansion programme brings together Business, Technology, Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, SHE, Finance and external partners to strengthen core chemistries and value chains. During FY26, this integrated approach supported projects designed to increase capacity, improve asset efficiency and build manufacturing resilience while balancing safety, sustainability and capital discipline.
Every project is evaluated for lifecycle value, not only initial cost. Three levers support this approach:

Reimagining Processes: Safer, Smarter, Sustainable 
Cross-functional teams combine chemistry, engineering, operations, digital capability and SHE expertise to redesign 
processes for better safety, efficiency and environmental performance. Key interventions during FY26 included:
Converting diazotisation and hydrolysis from batch to 
continuous processing to improve process safety.Converting the Halex process from batch 
to semi-batch.
Improving workforce stability through trained frontline 
teams and clearer ownership.Exploring mechanical vapour recompression to reduce 
steam consumption in key distillation columns.
Using Scaleban in cooling towers with RO reject water 
to conserve freshwater and improve water efficiency.Strengthening monitoring through RTMI and deploying 
visualisation by shifting selected dashboards from 
Google Sheets to Tableau.
Replacing washer-settler systems with liquid-liquid extraction columns to improve separation efficiency and reduce 
effluent generation.
Operational responsibility extends beyond how 
products are manufactured to how their risks, safe use and impacts are communicated across the value chain.By bringing together process 
knowledge, operating experience, safety considerations and digital capability, these interventions support safer operations, higher resource productivity and more resilient manufacturing.
Responsible Labelling: Informed Choices 
Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Product Stewardship and customer-facing teams work together to communicate product hazards, safe-handling requirements and relevant environmental and social information through labels and technical documentation. This integrated process supports regulatory compliance, safer handling and informed decision-making across the value chain. During FY26, the Company received 15 labelling-related complaints, with no reported instances of non-compliance or fines.
This responsibility continues after a product leaves the manufacturing site, 
requiring coordinated action among logistics teams, transporters, drivers and emergency-response partnersAIL reported no 
instances of  non-compliance with applicable product-labelling and marketing-information requirements during FY26.

Secure Storage. Safe Transport. Seamless Distribution
The safe movement of chemicals depends on coordinated action across manufacturing sites, logistics teams, transport 
partners, drivers, control-centre personnel and emergency-response networks. The Aarti Logistics Control Centre monitors a network of 1,000+ vehicles carrying approximately 350 chemical variants, supported by GPS-based tracking, route-risk controls and proactive incident response.
By extending operating standards and safety capability beyond the plant boundary, AIL treats transport partners as 
participants in responsible manufacturing rather than only as service providers. Together, these controls protect employees, communities, customers and the environment while supporting reliable delivery.
Reliable delivery must be matched by consistent product performance, making quality a shared responsibility across

Future Forward: Our Roadmap for Competitive, Sustainable Growth Future Forward: A Competitive and Sustainable Manufacturing Roadmap
Eight Priorities for Future Growth
Project Execution, Reimagined for a Sustainable Tomorrow Our quality transformation goes beyond products to building a sustainable future. By integrating people, processes, 
and technology into a future-ready system, we position quality as a driver of environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and stakeholder value.AIL’s five-year manufacturing roadmap builds on the progress achieved by integrating assets, people, technology and partner capabilities. It is designed to strengthen competitiveness, reliability, sustainability, and customer responsiveness by combining manufacturing experience with digital capability, advanced engineering, process innovation, and coordinated action across employees, technology partners, suppliers, and customers.
AIL follows a four-phase, stage-gated project-management process from concept to commissioning. Project, Technology, Engineering, Procurement, SHE, Manufacturing, and execution partners work together from the initial transfer of technical documents, preliminary design, and CAPEX estimation through detailed engineering, procurement, fabrication, erection, testing, and commissioning. This integrated approach improves safety, cost control, schedule certainty and plant operability.Quality Initiative Benefit/Impact

Recognising the importance of sustainability, the Company invested in a technology-driven Energy Management System 
(EnMS) to improve efficiency. By monitoring critical electrical data, the system optimises consumption and production while generating actionable insights.
These initiatives delivered energy savings of 2.3 million kWh, amounting to ` 2.3 Crs in FY26. ISO 50001:2018 certification 
across all divisions reinforces the Company’s commitment to optimising energy demand and supply.
For the medium term (2023-28), Aarti Industries Limited aims to reduce specific energy consumption by 20% from  
FY20 levels and source 25% of total energy from renewables. These targets support SDGs 11, 12, and 13 while reinforcing the 
Company’s commitment to preserving natural capital through collective progress.
During the reporting period, AIL’s total energy consumption increased to 9.23 million GJ from 8.08 million GJ in FY25. Renewable energy in its total energy mix decreased to 2.09% from 2.49% in FY25. This decrease is due to a 14% increase in energy consumption on account of a 19% increase in production.
The Company reduced specific energy 
consumption from 10.10 GJ/MT in FY20 to 7.52 GJ/MT in FY26.

Effluent Management
Non-recyclable wastewater 
undergoes 100% in-house tertiary treatment through advanced Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), enabling reuse or further treatment. Treated water quality is reported to authorities to ensure compliance. Effluent discharge increased from 283,047 KL in FY25 to 359,336 KL in FY26 due to 19% higher production. As part of the Company’s Environment 
& Climate Change Policy, the Company commits to no gross deforestation within its own operations and encourages its business partners (Suppliers) to adopt the same approach through engagement and awareness initiatives.
The Company avoids operations in 
ecologically sensitive areas and critical habitats of national or international importance and promotes biodiversity conservation through sustainable land management practices.
The policy is endorsed by Mr. Rajendra 
V. Gogri, Chairman & Managing Director and member of the Board of Directors, demonstrating Board-level oversight and commitment to environmental stewardship.Biodiversity risk assessments were conducted across 16 manufacturing units in Maharashtra and Gujarat using the WWF Biodiversity Risk Filter, as well as within a 10 km radius of project sites in accordance with the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006. The assessments indicated low exposure to risks associated with protected areas and sensitive ecosystems. Findings are integrated into the Company’s enterprise risk management framework.
AIL ensures environmental compliance through a third-party IT-enabled system, CMS (Compliance Management System) 
tracking licences, renewals, and obligations, with applications initiated at least 90 days before expiry.
Internal audits and independent reviews support governance, with environmental risk assessments completed at all sites 
and no significant fines in FY26. Targeted training further strengthens awareness and compliance practices.
Aarti Industries Limited continues 
to strengthen its environmental agenda through Zero Liquid Discharge systems, improved chemical recycling through its joint venture with Re Sustainability, and circular economy practices. The Company also works with clean-tech innovators and academic institutions to develop low-carbon and bio-based technologies. Our Commitment Biodiversity Risk Assessment
Environmental ComplianceBiodiversity and Ecosystem Protection
Advancing Environmental 
ResponsibilityAt AIL, we are committed to 
protecting and enhancing biodiversity by integrating nature-related considerations into our business operations and decision-making. We assess biodiversity risks and potential impacts associated with our manufacturing sites and projects, conserve and enhance natural habitats through green belt development and restoration initiatives, and implement robust pollution prevention measures to protect air, water, and soil quality. We promote sustainable water stewardship through efficient water management, recycling, reuse, and responsible wastewater treatment, while adopting sustainable land management practices to minimise ecological disturbance. We encourage responsible sourcing of raw materials with due consideration for biodiversity impacts across our value chain and undertake measures to protect local flora and fauna around our operations. Our climate action initiatives, including energy efficiency and renewable 
energy adoption, contribute to reducing 
pressures on ecosystems, while employee awareness programmes and community engagement initiatives foster environmental stewardship. We regularly monitor biodiversity-related 
indicators and continuously strengthen 
our environmental management systems through measurable objectives, regulatory compliance, and transparent governance to support the long-term conservation of biodiversity and sustainable development.
This is intended to be a long-term and 
ongoing commitment and therefore does not have a defined end date or target year for full implementation. The commitment is already integrated into the Company’s operational practices and will continue to apply throughout the Company’s operations.Deforestation, habitat loss, resource overuse, and climate change are recognised as key drivers of extreme weather risks. Biodiversity conservation is supported through responsible decisions, research, and best practices.
All manufacturing units are located in 
Notified Industrial Zones which are not 
situated near any ecologically sensitive Enriching Biodiversity
In FY26, we planted 
approximately 50,000 trees across Gujarat and Maharashtra as part of our afforestation  internally and externally. area, reducing ecological impact from 
our operations on biodiversity. None of the species listed in the IUCN Red List as threatened or at risk of extinction are found near our manufacturing locations. Green belts have also been developed around sites and in nearby areas in line with regulatory norms.
The assessment evaluates both biodiversity-related impacts arising from operations and dependencies on ecosystem services that support business continuity. Impact-related risks assessed include proximity to Protected Areas and Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs), ecosystem integrity, habitat condition, biodiversity sensitivity and land-use pressures. Dependency-related risks assessed include ecosystem services such as water availability, climate regulation, flood regulation, soil retention and natural resource availability.Assessment outcomes are used to identify, prioritize and manage nature-related risks and opportunities across the Company’s operational footprint, supporting informed decision-making and biodiversity conservation efforts.
In line with the Environment and 
Climate Change Policy, deforestation and expansion in ecologically sensitive areas are avoided. Animal welfare principles are upheld, and testing is conducted only when required by regulation, with no such instances in FY26.
Alongside this, our focus on responsible sourcing, renewable energy adoption and carbon capture supports emissions reduction across the value chain. Together, these initiatives reflect our ambition to build a future-ready and environmentally responsible specialty chemicals business.

Balz–Schiemann, and vapour phase technologies, we develop differentiated products for agrochemicals, polymers, energy materials, and performance additives.
R&D Evolution: Legacy that Set the Foundation
From complex chemistry commercialisation to green molecule development and customer-driven innovation, our R&D is guided by a clear principle: Design with the end in mind: sustainable, scalable, safe, and stakeholder-aligned processes.
We have evolved from traditional technology management to an innovation-led model, translating ideas from lab to market.

Commitment to Responsible Chemical Management for utilisation of hazardous substance: We are committed to 
minimising, restricting, and where feasible, eliminating the use of hazardous substances that may pose risks to human health and the environment. We comply with all applicable national and international regulations governing the manufacture, handling, storage, transportation, use, and disposal of hazardous chemicals, including relevant Indian regulatory requirements and globally recognised frameworks where applicable. Our approach emphasises responsible chemical management across the entire product life cycle, from raw material sourcing and manufacturing to distribution, use, and end-of-life disposal. We continuously assess opportunities to substitute hazardous substances with safer alternatives, strengthen operational controls, enhance employee awareness and training, and implement robust risk management practices to prevent environmental releases and occupational exposure. Through periodic monitoring, regulatory compliance reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives, we strive to reduce the environmental and health impacts associated with hazardous substances while ensuring safe and sustainable operations.

Generative AI and Agentic AI
To boost the productivity of individuals and improve the TAT, We are using Gemini tool, NotebookLM, Workspace studio and Google Enterprise Agent platform. Here, we do not have a dedicated AI-access policy, but access is genuinely controlled through the platforms themselves: Google Workspace rule-based access management, usage, model selection, connectors, and plug-ins. While using these images generated through Google’s tools (Gemini/Imagen) carry SynthID an invisible watermark plus C2PA-style metadata. NotebookLM Audio Overviews also carry SynthID. For custom use cases, we consume foundation models, we do not train your own, so classic statistical ‘drift monitoring’ does not really apply, the vendor owns model performance. What we do have is model-selection governance: ensuring we’re on enterprise/configured models rather than consumer versions, with the ability to control and change model versions over time. Performance Management and Career Development
AIL’s Management by Objectives approach collaboratively sets individual goals across business performance, sustainability, partner delight and people well-being. Bi-annual HRMS appraisals and agile monthly conversations enable continuous feedback and development. The multidimensional assessment considers Company values and individual contributions to team performance, ensuring transparent, holistic evaluation. The Company complies with applicable legal requirements relating to employee consultation and notice periods in the event of significant workforce restructuring.
CASE STUDY
REPURPOSING INTERNAL TALENT AT ZONE IV
Repurposing internal talent 
for the new Zone IV at Jhagadia was a strategic investment in continuity and long-term capability building. By prioritising employees with a deep understanding of the business and culture, the Company enabled a faster, more stable ramp-up of the greenfield project. Over 90% of manager-and-above roles were filled internally.High-potential employees were 
identified through organisation-wide talent mapping and succession reviews. Targeted talent spotting, internal job postings, and leadership discussions unlocked advancement paths for critical roles like Plant Manager, Division Head, and Mechanical Operations Head.This approach reinforces the Company’s commitment to developing future-ready leaders from within, positioning internal talent as a cornerstone of sustainable growth and strategic expansion.
Digitisation and Adoption of AI
Aligned with the evolving business landscape, the Company’s digitisation journey is enhancing agility, accuracy and transparency. 
Fully digitising reimbursements has reduced turnaround time from 45 days to 7 days, improving efficiency and accountability.
AI-enabled goal setting converts employee inputs into clear, measurable SMART goals. A digital skill matrix assesses 
competencies, identifies gaps and assigns targeted development actions. Contract labour payroll digitisation has improved processing accuracy, compliance and payment timeliness, strengthening operational efficiency and governance.T28

Human Rights Due Diligence
A robust human rights due diligence process aligned with UNGP and SA8000 standards is maintained by the Company to 
identify risks across operations, supply chains, partnerships, and mergers.
It addresses key issues including child and forced labour, human trafficking, wages, discrimination, exploitation, freedom of 
association and right to collective bargaining, while also assessing legal penalties. The process incorporates stakeholders such as women, children, migrants, contract workers, indigenous peoples, and communities, integrating their concerns to build trust.
In FY26, 100% of manufacturing sites across 16 divisions were assessed on human rights. Third-party validation reported 
no major violations or corrective actions. A Zone-level risk register tracks all human rights risks.
Human Rights Training and Capability Building
The Human Rights Policy is communicated to all contracted personnel and reinforced through targeted training. Security teams undergo regular sessions on human rights, legal compliance, conflict resolution, soft skills, and crowd management. This is further supported by online refresher courses, with 100% completion achieved.
To further strengthen accountability, a Disciplinary Action Plan defines 
responses to violations, discrimination, and harassment, while deterring misconduct. All investigations are led by the CHRO, who also serves as the Ethics Officer.Steps for Due Diligence
Identification of Potential Human Rights Risks
The Company identified and assessed 
relevant human rights risks across its own operations, the value chain, acquisitions and mergers. We built a repository covering child labour, forced labour, privacy, discrimination, freedom  of association, bargaining rights and labour rights.Risk  Assessment
Risks are assessed based on their 
probability and severity and classified as high, medium, or low. Existing controls are then evaluated to determine residual risk.
Action Planning
Action plans are developed to address 
residual high-risk issues to prevent violations.Monitoring and Reporting
Progress is tracked through defined 
responsibilities, timelines, and metrics. The risk register is reviewed on an annual basis.

Aarti Industries Limited embeds its values of Care, Integrity and Excellence into its operations and people practices to uphold human rights across its workforce, business partners and communities. Its Board-approved People Policy and Human Rights Codes, aligned with the UN Guiding Principles, International Bill of Human Rights and ILO standards, guide employees, contractors, partners and communities.
AIL provides fair working conditions 
and supports rest, leisure and work-life balance. In compliance with applicable laws and Company policies, its Human Resource Management System (HRMS) monitors working hours, overtime and leave utilisation. Employees work within prescribed legal limits, receive eligible overtime compensation and are encouraged to use annual leave, while excessive working hours are managed to protect health, safety and well-being. The Company also ensures equal remuneration for men and women performing work of equal value and equitable compensation across its workforce.
These commitments extend across 
the value chain through the Supplier Code of Conduct, supported by ongoing guidance on ethical labour and responsible business conduct. Reporting Work-Related Hazards and Hazardous Situations
A safe and supportive work environment is reinforced through established reporting mechanisms for work-related hazards 
and unsafe conditions. Employees are trained on incident reporting procedures, enabling timely investigations, corrective actions and open reporting without fear of retaliation.
Process Safety
Process safety is critical to preventing incidents and reducing the risk of harmful substance releases. AIL follows rigorous safety protocols, conducts detailed risk assessments and maintains emergency response plans to protect employees and communities.
 The Process Safety team works closely with the Aarti Research and Technology Centre to integrate safety across product 
development, scale-up and manufacturing. Key areas include tacit knowledge sharing, long-term chemical storage studies, powder handling studies and in-house data generation on chemical reaction hazards, fire hazards and explosion risks.
 For new and existing powder handling operations, the Company conducts studies covering Minimum Ignition Energy, Minimum 
Autoignition Temperature of a Dust Cloud, Hot Surface Ignition Temperature of Dust Layers, powder resistivity and other relevant parameters.Hazard Reporting Channels

Through systematic risk and hazard assessments, internal inspections, and audits, AMS enables the pr oactive identification and

Identified risks are prioritised and integrated into action plans with defined responsibilities, measurable targets, and periodic reviews to drive effective risk mitigation and continuous improvement. The system also incorporates emergency preparedness and response measures while monitoring performance against established health and safety objectives.

HEALTH SERVICES  
@AIL 
AIL provides occupational and non-
occupational health services through a 12-member Medical Board and 24×7 Occupational Health Centre (OHCs) at each manufacturing site, staffed by qualified medical teams and equipped for emergency response.  Pre-employment and periodic medical examinations are conducted for employees and contract workers based on occupational risk exposure.
The NIRVANA well-being programme 
addresses physical, mental, emotional, social, financial and community well-being through awareness, preventive health camps, medical follow-ups and counselling. The Anahata Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) provides confidential support to employees and families. Health records remain secure and access-controlled; participation is voluntary where applicable and does not influence employment decisions.  AIL maintains the confidentiality of employees’ and workers’ personal health-related information through secure record management and access controls, with access restricted to authorised medical personnel and designated officials on a need-to-know basis. Participation in occupational health services, medical examinations, counselling, or well-being programmes is voluntary where applicable and is not used to influence employment decisions or result in any favourable or unfavourable treatment of employees or workers.
Risk Identification and 
Control
We assess risks across the lifecycle 
from design and development to manufacturing, handling, storage and distribution using HIRA, Process Hazard Analysis and Job Safety Analysis. Oversight is strengthened through technical studies such as Thermal Safety using DSC and RC1e, 
Safety Integrity Level studies, Quantitative Risk Assessment, barrier health monitoring, and internal and external audits. During the year, 100% of applicable sites underwent HIRA. Employees are encouraged to report near misses, unsafe acts and deviations through Behaviour Based Safety and the Deviation Management System.
Incident Reporting and 
Learning
AIL follows a structured incident 
reporting and investigation process to identify root causes, apply the hierarchy of controls and share learnings across units. Employees are trained to report work-related hazards, unsafe situations and unsafe working conditions without fear of retaliation.
AIL also empowers workers to 
stop any activity or operation they believe is unsafe. Learnings from incidents are integrated into the continuous improvement of the OHSMS.

Training Coverage
SUCCESS STORY 
Module-based Training for Shift In-Charges and DCS Executives
Shift In-Charges and DCS Executives play a critical role in ensuring safe, stable and efficient plant operations. 
Internal reviews showed that while they managed daily operations effectively, their exposure to key aspects of the Aarti Management System was limited. Production demands, troubleshooting and coordination responsibilities left little time to revisit structured management system expectations, risk frameworks and standardised practices. This created the possibility of variation in system-led decision-making across shifts.
Structured Intervention
To address this gap, AIL introduced a module-based training programme for Shift In-Charges and DCS Executives. Participants were relieved of their regular duties for 8 hours once every 4 months, enabling focused learning without operational distractions.
The programme covered four modules and more 
than 80 technical and system-related topics aligned with critical AMS elements. Over 400 employees were covered, with sessions repeated every four months to reinforce recall, consistency and application across shifts.Areas of Learning
The sessions strengthened understanding of critical process parameters, interlock logic, alarm management, deviation control and structured risk assessment in line with AMS expectations. Real plant scenarios and past incident case studies made the learning practical and relevant. Participants were encouraged to move beyond immediate troubleshooting and adopt a system-driven approach to process control, operating discipline and risk anticipation.
The initiative improved confidence, ownership and alignment with AMS requirements among  
Shift In-Charges and DCS Executives. By linking daily operating decisions with management system principles, it strengthened process discipline, enhanced operational reliability and reinforced a proactive safety culture across the organisation.IMPACTSystem Training

Programmes and Focused Interventions

From Purpose to Practice - Our CSR Policy
Every CSR initiative begins with understanding 
community priorities and aligning them with AIL’s purpose of creating shared value. They are guided by stakeholder engagement, aligned with our business values and implemented through partnerships with organisations that possess deep local knowledge and execution capabilities. AIL’s Board-approved CSR Policy 
guides community investments in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013. Together, these initiatives reflect AIL’s belief that meaningful social impact is created through responsible stewardship of resources, collaborative partnerships and continuous engagement with communities.
